question_text: The mean and variance of a binomial distribution are 4 and 3 respectively. Find the distribution and find P(X ≥ 1).

recall_prompt: Say how you would find the distribution and P(X ≥ 1) from the mean and variance — how you get q, p and n, and how the complement gives the probability.
insider_note: Two things are asked: the distribution itself, ¹⁶Cᵣ (3/4)¹⁶⁻ʳ (1/4)ʳ, must be written before P(X ≥ 1); and P(X ≥ 1) is the one subtraction 1 − (3/4)¹⁶, never a sum of sixteen terms.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Find n, p, q
steps.margin_note: First mark. Mean = np, variance = npq. Divide: q = npq/np = 3/4, so p = 1/4, and then n = 4/p = 16. Always find q first — the variance-over-mean division gives q, not p.

recall.must_convey: That np = 4 and npq = 3 give q = 3/4, p = 1/4 and n = 16.
accept: mean is n p equal to four and variance n p q equal to three so q is three by four p is one by four and n is sixteen
divide variance by mean to get q, then p is one minus q and n is mean by p
q three quarters, p a quarter, n sixteen
npq by np cheste q three by four, p one by four, n sixteen
n is sixteen with p one fourth

steps.why: A binomial distribution is fixed by n and p, and the two given numbers are exactly two equations in them. Dividing removes n and gives q directly.
common_mistakes: Taking npq/np = p instead of q.

steps.label: Write the distribution and P(X ≥ 1)
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The distribution is P(X = r) = ¹⁶Cᵣ (3/4)¹⁶⁻ʳ (1/4)ʳ. P(X ≥ 1) is 1 − P(X = 0), and P(X = 0) = qⁿ = (3/4)¹⁶. Leave the power as it is.
lines: The distribution is P(X = r) = ⁿCᵣ qⁿ⁻ʳ pʳ

recall.must_convey: That the distribution is ¹⁶Cᵣ (3/4)¹⁶⁻ʳ (1/4)ʳ and P(X ≥ 1) = 1 − P(X = 0) = 1 − (3/4)¹⁶.
accept: the distribution is sixteen C r into three by four to the sixteen minus r into one by four to the r, and P of X at least one is one minus three by four to the sixteen
write n C r q to the n minus r p to the r with n sixteen, then one minus q to the n
P of X greater than or equal to one is one minus P of zero which is one minus three fourths to the sixteenth
distribution sixteen C r q power sixteen minus r p power r, P X at least one is one minus q power sixteen
one minus three by four to the power sixteen
heard_as: three by four to the sixteen

steps.why: P(X ≥ 1) covers sixteen values, but its complement P(X = 0) is one term, and P(X = 0) = qⁿ because every trial must fail. Using the complement is the standard method for an 'at least one' question.
common_mistakes: Never writing the distribution, which the question asks for.
